title: Each admin panel on screen asks the server every minute, so under a hundred busy gyms can use up the free daily request limit for everyone
what: While the admin panel is in view, the Needs you check asks the server once a minute, and reads its other lists every five minutes. A desk that keeps the panel open through a 16-hour day makes over a thousand requests. The free Cloudflare plan allows 100,000 a day for all gyms together, so roughly 80 to 90 such desks fill it, and then every gym panel and member app stops answering until the day resets.
expected: The repeating checks stay well inside the shared daily limit as gyms grow, or the plan is moved before the limit is near, and what happens at the limit is written down.
how_often: every day once about 80 desks keep the panel open
fix_line: Slow the minute check or push alerts to the panel instead, and decide the plan move before growth reaches the limit

title: A web-page chat question stopped by a limit does not say whether the day ran out or the AI credits did
what: When a visitor question on the gym web page was not sent to the AI, the owner sees one note that says a daily limit or no AI credits left. The owner cannot tell whether to wait for tomorrow or buy credits.
expected: The note names which limit stopped it and what the owner can do about it.
how_often: each time a limit is hit
fix_line: Give the two cases their own note, with the next step for each
